transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
I'm here because I've been struggling with eating really huge amounts of food. When it happens, it feels like I completely lose control and just can't stop myself. I really need some help with this.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, taking laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of those things at all. I have never forced myself to throw up, used laxatives, or tried to fast or over-exercise afterward.
Have you recently experienced significant weight loss, or do you actively restrict your food intake to keep your body weight extremely low?
No, I haven't experienced any significant weight loss at all. I also don't restrict my food intake or try to keep my weight extremely low.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food occur, and how many months has this been going on?
This has been going on for about a year and a month now. On average, these eating episodes happen at least once a week.
During these eating episodes, do you experience things like eating much faster than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or feeling very guilty or disgusted with yourself afterward?
Yes, I definitely eat much faster than normal during those times. Afterward, I feel incredibly guilty, depressed, and disgusted with myself.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Binge-Eating Disorder: recurrent episodes of binge eating with a sense of lack of control, eating much faster than normal, experiencing intense guilt/disgust/depression afterward, occurring at least once a week for over a year, with no inappropriate compensatory behaviors or restrictive eating patterns (ruling out Bulimia Nervosa and Anorexia Nervosa). We have sufficient evidence to make a final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a distinct loss of control, occurring at least once a week for over a year. These episodes are associated with eating rapidly and experiencing intense guilt and disgust afterward. The absence of inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as purging, laxative use, or excessive exercise) rules out Bulimia Nervosa, and the lack of severe food restriction or low body weight rules out Anorexia Nervosa.
